referents.why: 'Him' is the object of 'questioned', masculine singular. Jesus is the one Pilate questions and the addressee of Pilate's speech.
'You' inside Pilate's question is second person, so it is the addressee of that speech: Jesus.
'to him' (autoi) is dative singular masculine: the one Jesus answers, which is Pilate.
'You' in Jesus's reply is second person inside his speech, so it is the addressee of that speech: Pilate, whose words he returns.

links.why: The participle answering is nested in the reply clause, as the grammar nests it.
What Jesus says is nested in the reply clause; kept, with the content link added below, per the rule that both apply.
Reverses the order: the answering comes after the questioning, not before it. The reply is the next turn, carried by the turn structure.
The question is what Pilate asked, the content of his questioning, not a separate event joined by and.
links.category: speech content read as a plain and

links.why: The separate-word connective before the reply ties the reply to the question it answers; it is not a cause or result.
Pilate's questioning is a saying clause and what he says is his question. Per R1 added alongside the turn.
Jesus says, and what he says is 'You have said so'. Per R1 added alongside the turn and the within link.

groups.why: Pilate is the sender of the question. The addressee was missing; Jesus is the one questioned.

The builder's sender w12 is not a candidate in this verse. The reply is Jesus's own speech (R2), so the sender is Jesus and the addressee is Pilate. The part is only what is said, cl4. The participle cl3 frames the reply and stays nested in cl2 by the within link, so it is removed from the parts.
groups.category: sender and addressee of a reply

none_fit.what: A reply to a question by the other party. No link type says answers, so the question-and-reply pair is carried only by the two turns.

none_fit.where: cl2 (the reply) against cl0 and cl1 (the question)
none_fit.what: A reply that answers a question; no link type marks an answer to a question.

cant_tell.what: whether answering to him (cl3) belongs to the turn
cant_tell.why: a turn has one frame, and the participle describes the act of replying rather than being said; left outside the turn as a within clause for review
